description: Scopebond Action Taxonomy v1 — the coding, GitHub, MCP and HTTP action types and their parameter bounds, an extension of the policy vocabulary. Version 1.1 adds the cloud, Kubernetes, database, secret, identity, messaging and work-item types a coding agent reaches through command-line tools and MCP servers; each action carries the taxonomy version that introduced it, and 1.0 types are unchanged. Version 1.2 adds software.install: software an agent installs or runs from outside the project, by any route, without a verdict. Parameters are carried under intent.params; bound-able parameters (boundable: true) may be constrained by an action_allowlist clause's param_bounds. This JSON is the machine source; the @scopebond/policy-schema README describes it. Money/commerce action types keep their existing gateway/demo shapes and are not redefined here.

actions.summary: A shell command executed by a coding agent's harness.

parameters.description: The raw command line, stored as a digest plus a redacted head, never in full.

parameters.name: cwd

parameters.name: args
parameters.description: The parsed argument vector, excluding the program.

actions.summary: Software a coding agent installs or runs from outside the project: a package, a script piped to a shell, a downloaded program, a cloned repository whose scripts it runs, a container image, or an MCP server added to a tool's settings. Detection only: it says what is installed and from where, never whether it is safe.

parameters.name: route
parameters.description: How it is installed: the package manager or runner, a script piped to a shell, a download that is run, a clone whose scripts run, a container pull or run, or an MCP server written into a tool's settings.

parameters.name: ecosystem
parameters.description: Where the name lives: a package registry, a container registry, a git host, a script or program fetched by URL, a remote MCP server, or unknown.

parameters.name: verb
parameters.description: What the command does with it.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The package, module, image or repository as the request names it (an npm or PyPI name, a Go module path, an image without its tag, host/owner/repo). Never a local path; omitted when the request names none.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The version, range, tag or digest as written (1.2.3, ^1, >=2,<3, latest, sha256:...); omitted when none is written.

parameters.name: source_url
parameters.description: The URL it comes from, as scheme, host and path: never credentials, a query or a fragment.

parameters.name: source_domain
parameters.description: The host it comes from: the URL's host, or the registry or index the command names (--registry, --index-url, an image's registry). Omitted when the command names none, since the tool's own settings choose it.

parameters.name: from_manifest
parameters.description: True when it installs what a manifest, lockfile or requirements file lists (npm ci, pip install -r ..., uv sync, docker compose pull): the packages are not in the request.

parameters.name: global
parameters.description: True when it installs for the whole computer rather than the project (-g, pipx, cargo install, go install, brew).

parameters.name: lifecycle_scripts
parameters.description: For npm, pnpm, yarn and bun: blocked with --ignore-scripts, else unknown.

parameters.name: auto_confirm
parameters.description: True when the command answers the runner's own install prompt for itself (npx -y, npm exec --yes).

parameters.name: executed
parameters.description: For a download: whether the same command line also makes it executable or runs it.

parameters.name: mcp_server
parameters.description: For an MCP server added to a tool's settings: the name it is configured under.

parameters.name: via
parameters.description: The program the install was read from (npm, pip, curl, git, docker, claude), or the settings file's tool.

parameters.name: derived_from
parameters.description: The action this one re-describes, recorded beside it in the same action group: the shell command, or the file write that changes a tool's settings.

parameters.name: risk_class
parameters.description: The risk class of this instance (sensitive).
